approach: Fix the ordering at the plan sort in plan.rs. Add `Plan::build_improving`, which wraps `build_capped`. It first raises an improvement request whose cause is recorded in 3 or more distinct jobs to urgent, in memory and never for a person-set item. It then walks the whole order once with a gap rule: never more than two non-improvement dispatches in a row while a ready improvement item is queued. Where a third non-improvement item would come next, the best-ranked ready improvement item moves into that slot. Every such slot goes in `Plan.turns`, so `athena plan` shows every turn and each drain replan reproduces the rest. Improvement requests are found by a pure athena-core function `hestia::improvement_of(records)` from recorded links, never from title text. The set is: open steward-channel requests (`steward::improvement_requests`); the open request that `repeated_causes` links to each repeated cause (error review); the `request_job` of every `ThroughputProposal` in the throughput review records (the design request); and the open requests that hold Hestia's own `Spec requirement: <id>` body line (spec review), found by the same line test Hestia already uses to avoid queuing a duplicate. The slowdown request has no recorded link, so it is named as not covered. The drain tracks `since_turn` so replans keep the gap. `athena plan` prints `turn` and `promoted` lines. The drain report lists the turns actually taken.

decisions.choice: Identify improvement requests with `hestia::improvement_of(&Records) -> Improvement`. It lists four kinds. (1) Open steward-channel jobs, from `steward::improvement_requests`. (2) The open `RepeatedCause.request` job of each cause from `repeated_causes` (error review). (3) The `request_job` of each `ThroughputProposal` in `records.throughput_reviews`, when that job is an open request (throughput design request). (4) The open request jobs that hold a line `Spec requirement: <id>` (spec review), via a small helper that applies the exact line test of `spec_request_is_open` (hestia.rs:677-686) and is shared with it. `cause_jobs[job]` is the largest `RepeatedCause.jobs.len()` of a cause the job addresses; other kinds get no entry. Not covered, and named as such in the plan, the doc comment and the CHANGELOG: the throughput slowdown request. Its only links are the title prefix `SLOWDOWN_MARKER` and the free-text `ThroughputReview.note`/commit subject (hestia.rs:1226-1229, 1509-1517; records.rs:2200-2203); `ThroughputReview` has no job field for it, and adding one changes records and filing. The doc comment of `improvement_of` states that a person's request which cites a repeated cause's introspection ids, or holds a spec line, counts as an improvement request, because the link is by citation and not by author.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 1 and 3. All four Hestia paths queue on channel `cli` through `Athena::queue` (hestia.rs:749 spec, 1662 throughput, error review 1993/2001/2071), and only `RequestQueue::apply` writes channel `steward`, so a channel marker misses Hestia. The throughput proposal records the job (`request_job`, records.rs:2160), so the link is a record field. The spec line is a structured body line Hestia itself matches on (hestia.rs:453-455, 677-686), not title text. `repeated_causes` already links each cause to the open request citing its introspections (hestia.rs:277-319) and counts distinct jobs (hestia.rs:355-363).

rejected.option: Mark improvement requests by channel `steward` alone
rejected.why: Misses every Hestia request, which is filed on channel `cli`.

rejected.option: Match request titles, such as the throughput or slowdown marker prefix or 'Fix the root cause of a repeated failure'
rejected.why: Fragile text matching; the finding forbids it. Slowdown is therefore left out and stated as not covered.

rejected.option: Add a slowdown job field to ThroughputReview, or change how Hestia files
rejected.why: Out of scope: it changes records and filing, which the brief excludes.
The accepted reading says Steward or Hestia; the throughput and spec requests have a recorded link and cost little to add.

decisions.choice: The slot rule is a gap rule over the whole order. Walk the untried positions with `gap = min(since_turn, 2)`. An improvement item resets gap to 0. At a non-improvement item with gap 2, move the first later improvement item that is untried and ready into that position. Ready means every in-plan dependency is tried or sits at an index before the slot. Record each item that sits in a gap-2 slot, moved or already there, as an `ImprovementTurn { id, position, moved }`. An improvement item that sits earlier at gap below 2 is not a turn. A candidate that is not ready is skipped, and the next position is retried.
decisions.reason: One pass over the whole order means `athena plan` shows every turn. After each dispatch the drain replans with `since_turn` advanced, and the same walk gives the same remaining order, so first-plan order equals dispatch order. A sliding gap of at most two satisfies 'at least one in every three dispatches' for overlapping windows. Tiers and groups stay intact apart from the moved items.

rejected.option: Move one item in the first window only
rejected.why: The printed plan lists one turn where the drain will take several.

rejected.option: A stateless rule that places an improvement item at index 2 on every build
rejected.why: The drain rebuilds before each wave (drain.rs:2986-2990), so the item would be pushed back each time and starve.

rejected.option: Interleave the whole order, every third entry
rejected.why: Reshuffles tiers and groups; the gap rule moves only items that are due.

rejected.option: Mark every dispatched improvement item as a turn
rejected.why: An item that ranked early on its own did not need the guarantee.

decisions.choice: Rebuild groups after the moves. A new group starts where the original group differs from the previous item's, and also before and after each moved turn item, which becomes a singleton.
decisions.reason: A wave under `drain_concurrent` dispatches a whole group. A moved item in its own group means the group before it holds at most two items, so the one-in-three share holds per item and not only per wave. The result is subsets of the original disjoint groups, so grouping stays valid.

rejected.option: Leave the groups as `build_with` made them
rejected.why: A group of six disjoint urgent items would dispatch together ahead of the improvement item.

decisions.choice: Apply the urgent promotion in memory before `build_capped`, only to improvement items that are not person-set and are below urgent, when `cause_jobs >= REPEAT_URGENT_JOBS` (3, a new constant in plan.rs). Record `RepeatPromotion { id, jobs, from }` in `Plan.promoted`. `athena plan` prints the later demotion beside the promotion when `Plan.demoted` shows the item was demoted from urgent.
decisions.reason: Caps and person-set semantics stay as they are (out of scope). A person's priority is never lowered or raised. `hestia::REPEAT_JOBS` (2, the filing threshold) is untouched. Only the error-review kind carries a cause count, so the throughput and spec requests get the turn but are never promoted.

rejected.option: Promote after the caps so promoted items are exempt
Write the promoted priority to a record
rejected.why: Not requested; keeps records and the round-trip test unaffected.
Out of scope: it would change when root-cause requests are filed.

decisions.choice: `Plan::priority_violations` skips a moved turn item when it looks for the earlier, worse-priority item.
decisions.reason: `prepare` turns each violation into a 'plan order contradicts priority' note (drain.rs:2202-2204), so every guaranteed turn would otherwise print a false note.

rejected.why: Duplicates the knowledge of who was moved.

risks.risk: The promotion happens before `[priority_caps]`, so a promoted request is demoted to high when person-set urgent items fill the urgent tier. 'Treated as urgent' then holds only when there is room.
risks.mitigation: The guaranteed turn does not depend on priority, so the request still runs within three dispatches. `athena plan` prints the promotion and the demotion together, a plan.rs test covers it, and the CHANGELOG states the limit. Changing the caps is out of scope.

risks.risk: Moving an item could put a dependent before what it needs, or break a disjoint group.
risks.mitigation: A candidate moves only when every in-plan dependency is tried or sits before the target slot. Splitting a group only makes subsets of a disjoint group. A test checks every dependency precedes its dependent on the moved plan.

risks.risk: A person's own request that cites a repeated cause's introspection id, or holds a `Spec requirement:` line, is treated as an improvement request, because these requests are found by link and not by author.
risks.mitigation: Accepted: this is the existing meaning of 'addresses a cause' in `addressing_request`. The `improvement_of` doc comment and the CHANGELOG say so. A person-set priority is never changed and the request gets only its share of turns. A test covers a request citing nothing (not listed).

risks.risk: The throughput slowdown request gets no guaranteed turn, though Hestia files it. It has no recorded link: only the title prefix and the free-text note.
risks.mitigation: Named in the plan, the `improvement_of` doc comment and the CHANGELOG, with a test that asserts it is not listed. Title matching is rejected, and a record field would change filing and records, which are out of scope. A later change can add a job field to `ThroughputReview`.

risks.risk: `repeated_causes` is O(introspections x groups) and runs on each replan.
risks.mitigation: `improvement_of` runs once per `prepare`, and only open requests are listed. The tests file a request through the real `error_review_backfill`.

risks.risk: `batches_for` puts items with no plan entry ahead of planned ones (drain.rs 2843-2853), so a few dispatches can precede the improvement turn.
risks.mitigation: Items with no plan entry still advance `since_turn`, so the next planned dispatch is the improvement item. The case already exists and is unchanged.

risks.risk: Under `drain_concurrent` a whole group dispatches at once, which could dilute the one-in-three share.
risks.mitigation: Moved turn items are singleton groups, and the `Shared` `drain_concurrent` test checks that an improvement item is among the first three starts.

risks.risk: A tried item that stays in the queue (failed or held) could distort the gap count.
risks.mitigation: The walk runs over the untried positions only, and `tried` items stay in place and are ignored. A test with a tried improvement item shows it is neither counted nor moved.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in plan.rs build 8 entries: six `Priority::Urgent` person-filed ids and two `Priority::Normal` Steward ids, with empty dependencies and touches. Case A uses `TierCaps::UNLIMITED`. Case B uses `TierCaps { urgent: 3, high: 10 }` with the six ids in `person_set`, so all six stay urgent. `Plan::build_improving` gets `Improvement { items: [s1, s2], since_turn: 0, .. }`. More cases: `since_turn` 2 puts an improvement item first; `since_turn` 1 puts it second; a tried improvement item is not counted. A simulation builds the plan from the full order, then removes the first dispatched id and rebuilds with the advanced `since_turn` and tried set, for 8 dispatches, and asserts the dispatch order equals the first build's `order`.
demonstrations.observes: `plan.order[..3]` contains a Steward id in cases A and B. `plan.turns` names both Steward ids at positions 3 and 6 (1-based) with `moved: true`. The same inputs through `Plan::build_capped` leave both Steward ids last. The simulated dispatch order equals the first plan's order. No more than two non-improvement ids sit between turns.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the gap rule the order is the six urgent ids and then both Steward ids, so the first-three assertion fails. Without `since_turn`, the replan simulation and the drain-level test in criterion 4 fail because the item is pushed back on each replan.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Plan::build_improving` (added by step 2). The `Improvement` value is a plain argument and no double is used. Plan entries are built with the struct-literal helper that the existing plan.rs tests use (exists). Nothing under test is inside a fixture.

demonstrations.method: Two layers. (a) hestia.rs `improvement_of` tests use the existing harness `athena_in`, `class`, `introspection` and `put` (hestia.rs:2508-2567). The error-review request is filed through the real path `athena.error_review_backfill` (as the tests at hestia.rs:3630-3712 do), so it lands on channel `cli` through `Athena::queue`. A failure class with introspections in jobs a, b, c gives `cause_jobs == 3`; a class with only a, b gives 2. A throughput record built with `request_job` set to an open request job (the way the existing throughput tests put a `ThroughputReview`) is listed, with no cause count; with the request closed it is not listed. A request queued with `athena.queue` whose text holds the line `Spec requirement: R1` is listed; the same text with the line absent is not. A plain person request citing nothing is not listed. A steward-channel `Request` (built as the fixture at hestia.rs:3354 does) is listed. A request closed by `athena close` is not listed. A slowdown request built with `slowdown_request` and queued is asserted NOT listed, which documents the gap. (b) plan.rs `repeat_urgent` tests pass `Improvement { cause_jobs: {h: 3} }` and an older normal entry to `build_improving`. A 3-job request is returned at Urgent, with `plan.promoted` holding `{jobs: 3, from: Normal}` and `h` ordered first. The 2-job case stays normal with `promoted` empty and the order by age. A `person_set` item is not promoted. With the urgent tier full of three person-set items, a promoted item is demoted to high and shows in both `plan.promoted` and `plan.demoted`.

demonstrations.seam: `Plan::build_capped` (exists) is the reference, and `Plan::build_improving` (step 2) is the code under test. The `Stub` in tests/drain.rs (exists) gets only the default `Steps::improvement()`, which returns an empty value.

demonstrations.method: tests/drain.rs: `Stub` gets an `improvement: Improvement` field (items and cause counts) and a `Steps::improvement` override that returns it. It holds 6 person-filed urgent entries and 2 improvement entries, one with cause count 3, with `person_set` and caps left at the `Steps` defaults. `drain::plan(&stub, 5.0, &Quiet)` gives a `PlanReport`, and `display::plan(&report)` is asserted to contain a `turn` line and a `promoted` line, each naming the id and title. A promoted-then-demoted case asserts the same line shows the demotion. A second test runs `drain::drain` with `max_jobs` 8 and asserts the `run` log order equals the `PlanReport` order from `drain::plan`, that `report.improvement_turns` names the improvement items that ran as turns, and that `display::drain(&report)` has an `improvement` line naming each with its job. The concurrent case runs `drain::drain_concurrent(&shared, limits(..), &Quiet, 3)` with the `Shared` double (tests/drain.rs:7183) after step 9 gives it the `improvement` field and override; it has 6 independent urgent items and 2 improvement items, and asserts an improvement id is among the first three `start` log entries and that no more than two non-improvement items start before it. A display.rs unit test builds a `PlanReport` and a `Report` by hand with non-empty `turns` and `improvement_turns`, and an empty one that prints neither line.
demonstrations.observes: The plan text contains a line like `turn        <id> · <title> takes the improvement turn` and a line like `promoted    <id> · <title>: cause recorded in 3 jobs, raised from normal to urgent`. The drain text names each item that took a turn. With no improvement items neither line appears, and the existing plan-text needles still match.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `turns`, `promoted`, the `Report` field and the display lines, the text has none of the needles and `report.improvement_turns` does not compile. With `build_capped` in place of `build_improving`, the concurrent first-three assertion fails, because all six urgent items start first.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `drain::plan`, `drain::drain`, `drain::drain_concurrent`, `display::plan` and `display::drain` (all exist). The injection is the `Stub` and the `Shared` double, each with a new `improvement` field and `Steps::improvement` override (added by steps 6 and 9; `Shared` is `Sync` because `Improvement` is plain data). The doubles only report which ids are improvement requests and their cause counts; the ordering and the report are production code.

demonstrations.method: plan.rs tests: (a) an improvement entry with no acceptance has `missing()` non-empty and is in `refused`; a ready improvement item behind it takes the turn. (b) An improvement entry depends on a job that `history` shows failed with no landed retry; it is held and in `refused`. (c) An improvement entry depends on an in-plan item that would sit at or after the target slot: it is skipped for that slot and takes a later one once its dependency has run; every dependency precedes its dependent in `order`. (d) With no ready improvement item, `turns` is empty and the order equals the `build_capped` order. (e) A moved turn item produces no `priority_violations` entry.
demonstrations.observes: `plan.turns` never names a refused, held or unready item. In every case a dependency precedes its dependent.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the walk accepted any improvement item, the refused or held item would appear in `plan.turns` or the dependent would run before its dependency, and the assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: `Plan::build_improving` with plain entries and `history` values (the `JobEnd` constructors that the existing hold tests in plan.rs use, which exist). The candidate filter is the production walk in plan.rs (step 2), not a double.

demonstrations.method: Read the new entry under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` and match each sentence to the diff. It states: the root cause (the drain ordered by person-set priority alone); the guaranteed turn (at most two other dispatches between improvement requests while a ready one is queued) for open steward-channel requests, the open request that cites a repeated cause's introspections (a person's request that cites them counts too), the throughput design request recorded as a proposal's `request_job`, and the open spec-review request; that the throughput slowdown request is not covered because no record links it; the raise to urgent for a cause recorded in three or more distinct jobs, made before `[priority_caps]` so a full urgent tier can demote it again, and never applied to a priority a person set; the `turn` and `promoted` lines in `athena plan`; the improvement line in the drain report; the new `Steps::improvement` method.
demonstrations.observes: Every sentence maps to a changed function or test, and nothing is claimed about the filing threshold, Hestia or Steward text, or caps.
demonstrations.fails_without: An entry that claimed more than the diff (for example the slowdown request being covered, or a change to the filing threshold or caps) would not map to a changed function or test.
